questions.question: During a Dive Deep, an engineer says 'BGP just picks the shortest path.' Your correction:
options: BGP is policy-driven; attributes (local-pref, AS-path, MED, etc.) decide path selection—not simple hop count
questions.explanation: Global NDE prep + InterviewStack: BGP decision process literacy.

questions.question: A candidate claims iBGP needs no loop prevention. Best pushback:
options: iBGP doesn’t re-advertise learned iBGP routes by default—hence route reflectors/confederations and AS-path for eBGP

questions.question: When would you prefer an IGP like OSPF/IS-IS inside a domain versus eBGP everywhere?
options: When you need fast interior convergence and topology awareness within an AS, accepting different operational tradeoffs than policy-heavy BGP
Always—BGP cannot be used in DCs

questions.question: Two 'redundant' uplinks share one optical system. As manager you flag:
options: Diversity failure: correlated risk means redundancy is partially illusory

questions.question: Elephant flows hashing to one ECMP member cause hot spots. Good engineering response:
options: Understand flow hashing limits; consider spraying/rehash strategies and capacity headroom—not assume perfect balance

questions.question: RIB looks healthy but packets blackhole. Most useful mental model:
options: Control plane (RIB) can diverge from forwarding/data plane (FIB/hardware)—validate actual forward path
questions.explanation: NDE prep: routing vs forwarding tables.

questions.question: Small pings work; large transfers stall mid-TLS. First networking hypothesis:
options: MTU/PMTUD black hole—large packets dropped along the path

questions.question: Why might TCP throughput stay low on a high-BDP path even with 'green' links?
options: Windowing, loss, buffering, and RTT interact—link up ≠ app goodput

questions.question: BFD is often paired with routing to:
options: Detect failures faster than hello timers alone, enabling quicker traffic shift—with CPU/false-positive tradeoffs

questions.question: Anycast helps services when:
options: Traffic steers to a nearby healthy instance and unhealthy announcements are withdrawn

questions.question: Customer overlay symptoms with healthy underlay metrics suggest:
options: Fault may be overlay control plane, encapsulation, or mapping—not only physical links
Underlay metrics prove overlay health always

questions.question: Stateful midboxes plus asymmetric routing often fail because:
options: Return traffic may bypass the state holder that saw the forward flow

questions.question: Asking 'life of a packet' from host A to B is valuable because it forces:
options: Layered path reasoning: L2/L3 hops, lookups, ACLs, encapsulation, and failure points

questions.question: CAM/TCAM pressure matters operationally because:
options: Forwarding/ACL scale limits can cause unexpected drops or slow-path behavior under growth

questions.question: Admin-up with zero errors but customers impacted implies:
options: Ignore customers if SNMP is green

questions.question: QoS under congestion is best framed as:
options: Prioritization that buys time—not a substitute for capacity and healthy topology
A permanent fix for undersized fabrics

questions.question: Route flaps hurt more than a clean fail-over because they:
options: Thrash forwarding and burn control-plane CPU repeatedly

questions.question: Minimum useful fabric telemetry set for Dive Deep:
options: Errors/drops, utilization, neighbor/session state, control-plane health, and synthetic probes
